name: How does the dry Colorado climate affect kitchen trim installation?

mainEntity.name: How does the dry Colorado climate affect kitchen trim installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Denver and nearby communities like Centennial, Parker, and Greenwood Village, the arid climate and seasonal humidity swings cause wood to shrink significantly in winter and expand during summer rains. Natural wood moldings must acclimate inside your home for several days before installation to prevent shrinkage gaps at mitered corners. Furthermore, homes in older Denver metro neighborhoods frequently experience settled framing, requiring extensive scribing and flexible elastomeric caulk that can tolerate structural shifting without cracking open.
acceptedAnswer.description: Dry Colorado air causes wood shrinkage, requiring several days of indoor acclimation prior to cutting, plus flexible caulk to handle seasonal movement.
